newsitem.title: GERMANY: SOCCER-KAISERSLAUTERN BEAT EVERTON TO SFORZA.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-KAISERSLAUTERN BEAT EVERTON TO SFORZA.

text.p: German first division side Kaiserslautern on Monday signed Internazionale's Swiss midfielder Ciriaco Sforza, beating England's Everton in the race to attract the player.
Kaiserslautern, who clinched promotion to the Bundesliga last season, said it had paid 6.5 million marks ($3.6 million) for Sforza who used to play for the German side.
The club added that he had signed a four-year contract and would join the team in pre-season training on Tuesday morning.
Sforza, who has earned more than 40 caps for his country and who took part in the 1994 World Cup, played for Kaiserslautern until 1995 before moving to Bayern Munich.
Everton had said earlier on Monday that they were close to signing Sforza from his Milan club.
It was reported at the weekend in Britain that the English premier league club had offered three million pounds ($5 million) for the Swiss player. ($ = 1.787 German Marks)
